2. The short facts, as alleged by the petitioner, upon which the aforesaid Rule was issued are, that the petitioner's minor daughter Sukla Rani Datta whose date of birth is said to be 5.2.76 was forcibly taken away from the petitioner's house by a few persons in the night following on 2.6.89 for which occurrence a Criminal Case in Boalmari Police Station has been started on 4.7.89 under section 364 of the Penal Code read with section 4(b)(c) of the Cruelty to Women (Deterrent Punishment) Ordinance, 1983 and the Special Powers Act, 1974. The victim girl along with her alleged abductor accused Musharraf Hossain (added O.P. No. 5) was arrested by Police and they were sent to custody on 4.7.89 by the Upazila Magistrate, Boalmari. The victim girl was thereafter sent for examination of her age on 5.7.89 to the Civil Surgeon, Faridpur who opined that she is aged about 18/19 years. 

 8. It is a simple case of the petitioner that his 4th child Shukla Rani Datta is a minor born on 5.2.76. His 5th child Kartick Chandra and the 6th child Kalipada Datta were born on 5.5.78 and 19.7.81 respectively. These three children were students of Solna Government Primary School reading in Class-V, IV and II respectively in the year 1989. Apart from the statements made on oath by the petitioner and his wife as to the date of birth of the girl and their two other children, as named above, the petitioner also produced school leaving certificates (Annexure-A, H and H-1) issued by the Head Master of Solna Government Primary School. To show that Musharraf Hossain was also a minor as on 5.2.89 (the alleged date of his marriage with the girl) the petitioner produced Registration Card No. 99276 of S.S.C. Examination issued by the Secondary Education Board, Dhaka and a certificate from the Head Master of Boalmari George Academy (Annexure I and J respectively) to the effect that the date of birth of Musharraf Hossain is 16.5.72. 

 10. Mr. Halder next submits that the statement of the minor girl as to her own age carries no weight at all. He also submits that no reliance should be placed on the medical report given by the Civil Surgeon as to the girl because the same is based on superficial observation and without taking any X-ray and Skiagram of the different joints of the body of the girl. Mr. Haider lastly submits that the police having found a prima facie case to the effect that on 2.6.89 Shukla Rani was only 13 years 4 months 3 days old, Musharraf Hossain and others committed an offence under section 364 of the Penal Code read with section 4(b)(c) and 9 of the Curelty to Women (Deterrent Punishment) Ordinance, 1983 and section 4(b) of the Special Powers Act, 1974 for kidnapping her and submitted charge-sheet against them on 11.11.89 in G.R. Case No. 42 of 89 which is still pending in the Court of Upazila Magistrate, Boalmari, Faridpur. 

 11. The contrary case of the girl herself and that of her alleged husband Musharraf Hossain is that the girl was major on 5.6.89 and she, out of her free will, embraced Islam and took the Muslim name Mst. Fatema Khatun and voluntarily married Musharraf Hossain on 5.6.89 under a Kabinnama. Their further case is that the girl being sui juris is legally entitled to marry any one of her choice and to be in the custody of her lawfully married husband. 

 14. To support their contentions Mr. Abdul Baset Majumder and Mvi. Md. Wahidullah have cited the decisions reported in AIR 1933 (Cal) 632, 15 DLR (Dhaka) 148 and 3 unreported decisions of this Court in Writ Petition No. 63 of 1982 and Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos. 31 of 1983 and 57 of 1984. 

 15. In the absence of a nuetral home in our country for unfortunate allegedly kidnapped immature girls, the moot point in this case for determination is the age of the girl that is, whether the girl is sui juris (a person having full legal capacity to act) or not on the facts alleged and proof furnished, because in essence it is a case for custody of the girl Shukla Rani Datta and hence her majority or minority will be the deciding factor to allow her to go wherever she likes or to give her to the custody of her lawful guardian. In this connection reference may be made to the decision in the case of Sukhendra Chandra Das Vs. Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs and others, reported in 42 DLR (HCD) 79 (in which one of us was a party) and the case of Monindra Kumar Malakar Vs. Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs and others reported in 1990 BLD (HCD) 85 wherein two different views were taken regarding the age of the minor for the purpose of deciding the question of custody of the person of the minor girl. In the case of Sukhendra Chandra Das 42 DLR 79 it was held as follows: 

 16. In the case of Monindra Kumar Malakar 1990 BLD 85 it was held that as the father of the detenu girl has failed to prove that the detenu girl was less than 16 years of age, the detenu girl cannot be kept in custody and is allowed to go anywhere she likes observing as follows:— 

 "If father claims guardianship, then it is not under section 366 A(of the Penal Code) rather the relevant section is 361 of the Penal Code (Bangladesh) where the girl is treated minor if she is found below 16 years If the girl is found below 16 years and if she is taken away without consent of the guardian, then it will be an offence and the guardian is entitled to have the custody of the minor girl   In a case like this when guardian prays not only for declaration of illegal detention but also claims the custody of the girl on the ground of minority, section 491 of the Code of Criminal Procedure shall be read along with section 361 of the Penal Code." 

 17. It has been decided in the case of Muthu Ibrahim Vs. Emperor, reported in ILR 37 Mad 567 that for the purpose of lawful guardianship the age of majority is that as laid down in section 3 of the Majority Act/1875. Though a Mohamadan female attains majority upon her attaining puberty under Mohammadan Law, she is still a minor and subject to the control of the guardian till she attains majority, that is, till she becomes sui juris according to the Majority Act, 1875. 

 18. We are in respectful agreement with the views expressed in Muthu Ibrahim's case ILR 37 Mad 567 and in the case of Sukhendra Chandra Das 42 DLR 79 that for the purpose of custody of the girl age of majority laid down in the Majority Act 1875 read with Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 i.e. the age of 18 years is the determining factor to decide whether the girl is to be given to the custody of the guardian or she is major. It is needless to state that reference to the age of sixteen in case of a female minor in section 361 of the Penal Code is only for the purpose of commission of the offence of kidnapping punishable under section 363 of the Penal Code and not for the purpose of deciding whether the girl is sui juris. 

 19. The petitioner placed his and his wife's statements on oath that the girl's date of birth is 5.2.76. To corroborate their assertion they produced school-leaving certificate from the Head Master of the School where the girl was reading. On the other hand, the girl herself asserts that she is major, has embraced Islam and married her lover Musharraf Hossain out of her free will. In support of her claim she filed an affidavit, the kabinnama dated 5.6.89 and the Medical Report dated 5.7.89. Now at this preliminary stage of the case without any prejudice to the case of the parties, it is for us to accept one set of proof prima facie in preference to the other according to our satisfaction. 

 20. We will now proceed to consider the proof furnished by the parties as to the age of the girl. In a case reported in AIR 1916 (PC) page 242, Lord Shaw observed:— 

 It has been observed in the case reported in 28 DLR 123 that the medical evidence as to age of a person cannot be utilised to override the effect of other cogent evidence on the point and my Lord Mustafa Kamal, J., while his Lordship was in the High Court Division, observed, with approval of the aforesaid decision, in his Lordship's judgment dated 22.7.84 in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.31 of 1983 and 1 of 1984 as follows:— 

 "We shall, therefore, have no hesitation in rejecting the medical evidence on record in this case if we are satisfied that there are other cogent evidence on record which overrides the medical evidence." 

 24. Having observed the girl when she was produced before this court and having heard her statements (by one of us), this court was not convinced that she looked like a fully developed adult 'Woman and intelligent enough to understand and decide her own well-being. Although nothing was recorded in the courts order to that effect but it is obvious from the fact that she was sent back to the Judicial Custody wherefrom she was produced before this Court. We have no hesitation in our mind to say that in the preliminary stage of the pending criminal case some credence should be given, in appropriate cases, to the statement of the parents in determining the age of a child. In the facts and circumstances, of the present case we are inclined to accept the parent's version as to the age of the girl. 

 25. To prove that Musharraf Hossain was minor on 5.6.89, the petitioner produced Annexure-I and J the genuineness whereof has neither been challenged by Musharraf Hossain nor he produced any paper to prove to the contrary. His learned Advocate also advanced no argument to negate the argument of Mr. Halder that Musharraf Hossain was a minor on 5.6.89 (the date of his alleged marriage with Shukla Rani Datta). So, the principle of admission by nontraverse will apply in this case. 

 26. For the reasons stated above we take the prima facie facie view that the date of birth of Shukla Rani Datta is 5.2.76, that is, she was and till today is prima, a minor being 14 years 1 month 5 days old as on today. We also find that Musharraf Hossain being born on 16.5.72 was, prima facie, facie, a minor on the date of alleged marriage on 5.6.89. This view of ours will however, not prejudice the other party's right to prove to the contrary by cogent evidence at the trial. Since the girl is prima facie a minor aged only about fourteen years her refusal to go with the parents is not at all material so far as her custody and well-being are concerned. It is the parents who are the best persons to get custody of their minor children in the facts and circumstance of the case. 

 27. We have carefully gone through the decisions cited by Mr. Abdul Baset Majumder and Mvi. Md. Wahidullah but find that in all the cited decisions the Court came to the clear findings that the detenus were not minors. But in the instant case we have prima facie found the girl to be a minor. So, these decisions are not applicable in the facts and circumstances of the present case.
